BiblicalUsage: The name is a river and a mountain. Abana, the river of Damascus, is the water Naaman wants to wash in instead of the Jordan, and he turns away in a rage before his servants talk him back; and Amana is the mountain the bride is called to look from, from the top of Amana, from Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens; one name, two places, and the Bible keeps them apart by the story.
TheologicalSignificance: A name shared by a river and a mountain carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the two scenes, that a proud general nearly missed his healing over a river and a bride is called to look out from a height.
